blockers.quote: (Every purchase until the repayment night is on a tab or a promise, every payment deferred to the repayment night, so the balances on the counter stay the clean powers of two.)
blockers.why: #5 But / therefore fails: no money is spent, yet the next beat raises local prices and the turn later says, "You spend here." The consequence has no cause.
blockers.fix: Defer purchases only through day thirty-one. Then have you actually clear the pier's tabs and pay local suppliers; show rounded balances thereafter, and move the first price rise to the following morning.

blockers.quote: Every midnight, your money doubles. A month ago you looked at that screen before you ordered this coffee. This morning you could buy the coffee, the kiosk, the pier, the street behind it and the ship coming in.
blockers.why: #3 Second hook by 0:30 fails at the stated pace: the cold open contains roughly thirty seconds of speech before the separate premise question, so its 0:20 endpoint is impossible.
blockers.fix: Replace the spoken opening with: "Mrs. Vance: What is that? Theo: Day thirty-one. Every midnight, your bank balance doubles. This morning it passed a billion dollars. You can buy this coffee, this kiosk, this pier—and tonight it doubles again." Then ask the premise question before 0:25.

blockers.quote: The last square alone holds 9,223,372,036,854,775,808 grains; the whole board 18,446,744,073,709,551,615 (c07).
blockers.why: #7 Misconception first fails its one-number-at-a-time requirement: the beat stacks square numbers and two enormous totals before either can land.
blockers.fix: Keep one spoken magnitude: "The last square alone holds nine quintillion grains (c07)." Cut the square-thirteen, square-thirty-three and whole-board totals from narration; let the cup, kiosk, pier and city show the progression.

suggestions.quote: Mr. Halloran, bored, emails him the loan-payoff batch template, including the creditor account map it requires.
suggestions.fix: Make the early interface limited and auditable, with Halloran refusing broader access; his second call can unlock the global run because the deadline changes his decision.

suggestions.quote: If you refuse, their money breaks by morning.
suggestions.fix: Give refusal a defensible side: establish that the balance cannot repay every debt, so every ordering rescues some borrowers and excludes others without consent; make that allocation cost someone named.

suggestions.quote: A chessboard chalked on the counter, one grain of rice on square one, doubled on each
suggestions.fix: Beat the familiar chessboard demonstration by translating its progression into the premise's port world—cups, sacks, containers and ships—while retaining only the final chessboard fact.
